svg.text: Manufacturing Intelligence - ask a database in plain English
Text-to-SQL + RAG assistant on demo data. One switch in .env chooses the classic pipeline or the LangChain pipeline; the safety parts are always our own code.
History: every question with its SQL,
Use their OWN LLM - no Groq tokens of ours
run_sql refuses known SQL mistakes with an
error the other LLM must fix
the 4 MCP tools, same search + guard + MySQL
agent.py - the orchestrator: one question, step by step
problem or MySQL error -> the LLM fixes the SQL (max 3 tries)
USE_LANGCHAIN in .env: off (default) -> classic | on -> LangChain
groq client - the 3 AI calls (rewrite, SQL, answer)
the default - what the main project uses
Always our own code, in both versions
sql_guard.py (one SELECT, allowed tables, max 500 rows) · warehouse.py (read-only, 30 s) · date rules + checks · retry loop · tokens + time box
star schema: dim_* and fact_* (invoices, sales
chats, questions, SQL, tokens, step times
backup qwen at the daily limit
OFFLINE - loading the data and the knowledge (run by hand)
cleans the input files -> MySQL ai_gold (star schema)
one chunk per ## section -> embed -> Qdrant mi_docs
PyPDFLoader + text splitter -> embed -> Qdrant mi_pdfs
document question -> answer from the PDFs, with file + page
Live check: same SQL and numbers both ways
Python · Django · MySQL · Qdrant · FastEmbed · Groq · LangChain · sqlglot · MCP · Docker · pytest
Every number comes from the database; the LLM only writes SQL and explains the rows. If the data cannot answer, it says so.
